columns.name: row_id
columns.note: numeric integer; joined to the private truth by row_id — must cover every row_id in the held-out test set (98 rows); no duplicate values allowed; the extractor may remap agent row numbering to the canonical row_id list from data/test.xlsx

columns.name: conductivity
columns.note: predicted ionic conductivity; must be numeric, non-null, and finite; units are the agent's responsibility (task spec: 1e-4 S/cm); do NOT rescale or alter the predicted value

columns.name: activation
columns.note: predicted activation energy (Ea); must be numeric, non-null, and finite; do NOT alter the predicted value

columns.name: density
columns.note: predicted relative density; must be numeric, non-null, and finite; units are the agent's responsibility (task spec: %); do NOT alter the predicted value

structural_checks: file submission.csv must exist at the root of submission_dir
all four columns [row_id, conductivity, activation, density] must be present — column names are matched verbatim, no aliases and no fuzzy matching
every value in all four columns must be parseable as a number (pd.to_numeric with errors='coerce' must yield no NaN)
conductivity, activation, and density must all be finite (np.isfinite check across the whole block)
row_id must contain no duplicate values
the set of row_id values must be a superset of every row_id in the private truth file — i.e. all 98 test rows must have a prediction
